<jats:p>
                    In this article we construct a p-adic three-dimensional eigenvariety for the group
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X1900736X_inline1"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$U$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    (2,1)(
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X1900736X_inline2"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$E$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ), where
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X1900736X_inline3"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$E$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    is a quadratic imaginary field and
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X1900736X_inline4"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$p$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    is inert in
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X1900736X_inline5"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$E$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . The eigenvariety parametrizes Hecke eigensystems on the space of overconvergent, locally analytic, cuspidal Picard modular forms of finite slope. The method generalized the one developed in Andreatta, Iovita and Stevens [
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X1900736X_inline6"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$p$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    -
                    <jats:italic>adic families of Siegel modular cuspforms</jats:italic>
                    Ann. of Math. (2)
                    <jats:bold>181</jats:bold>
                    , (2015), 623–697] by interpolating the coherent automorphic sheaves when the ordinary locus is empty. As an application of this construction, we reprove a particular case of the Bloch–Kato conjecture for some Galois characters of
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="gif" xlink:type="simple" xlink:href="S0010437X1900736X_inline7"/>
                        <jats:tex-math>$E$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , extending the results of Bellaiche and Chenevier to the case of a positive sign.
                  </jats:p>
title: Families of Picard modular forms and an application to the Bloch–Kato conjecture
